questions.q: According to the summary, what change brought about monogamy?
a: Settling down to farm and own land
The rise of hunter-gatherer tribes
The invention of religious law
The growth of modern cities
questions.why: Lesson 1 ties marriage and monogamy to the shift from foraging to farming.

questions.q: Why did men want certainty about which children were theirs?
a: To pass on the prosperity they had built
To avoid paying taxes on extra children
To keep their wives from working
To follow the rules of their religion
questions.why: Lesson 1 says inheritance made proof of fatherhood matter.

questions.q: What did the arousal studies in the summary find?
a: Men and women were aroused equally by erotic films
Men were aroused much faster than women
Women responded only to romantic scenes
Arousal depended mostly on the viewer's age
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes studies measuring arousal across men and women.

questions.q: How did most women describe their own arousal in those studies?
a: They downplayed how aroused they were
They overstated how aroused they were
They refused to answer any questions
They reported feeling no arousal at all
questions.why: Lesson 2 says women tended to play down their arousal when asked.

questions.q: Which body feature does the summary treat as evidence of sperm competition?
a: Testicles placed outside the body for cooler sperm
Men having deeper voices than women
Women having wider hips than men
Humans having less body hair than apes
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists several physical traits, starting with testicles kept outside the body.
